headline: US markets sold off hard last night with the NASDAQ down 1.8%, Iran-Strait of Hormuz tensions rattled oil markets, and the Roosters clinched the NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights in a thriller.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dropped 3.1% last night in a broad NASDAQ sell-off. There's no specific bad news — in fact GTA 6 rumours suggest it's tracking close to 15 million copies sold and $1.5B in revenue, and Rockstar is reportedly adapting the engine for Nintendo Switch 2. The long-term GTA 6 story remains very much intact.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 2.5% last night as the broader NASDAQ took a hit, dragging tech stocks down across the board. There's no specific Google news today — this looks like market-wide selling pressure rather than anything company-specific. Long-term thesis unchanged.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped 1.8% today, following weakness in US tech stocks from last night's NASDAQ sell-off. AI ETFs tend to mirror big US tech moves, so this is a ripple effect rather than any new problem. The fund is down 16.6% overall from your cost base — a rough patch for the AI sector this year.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell 1.4% today — emerging markets (think China, India, Brazil) tend to get hit when the Aussie dollar weakens and when global risk appetite sours. The AUD fell 0.8% against the USD last night, which adds a bit of extra drag on this fund's underlying assets.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara bounced 1.05% today — a small positive session in what's been a very rough longer-term ride (down 57% from your cost base). Lithium sector sentiment remains uncertain, with headlines today citing ongoing uncertainty clouding the outlook. No fundamental change today, just a mild uptick.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF dipped 0.33% today — a minor move in line with the broader ASX 200 falling 0.4%. Nothing specific to this ETF; it just tracks global equities broadly so when markets dip slightly, so does it. You're still fractionally in the green overall on this one.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped 0.36% today, tracking the mild ASX weakness. No specific news — this is a diversified multi-asset ETF and tiny daily moves like this are just normal background noise. Long-term story is solid.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down 0.23% today on the ASX, though the underlying US market sold off harder last night (S&P down 1.3%). The ASX-listed price didn't fully reflect last night's US weakness — that may catch up when the US opens tonight. You're up 6.1% overall on this one.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was essentially flat last night, barely moving while the rest of the NASDAQ sold off — a sign of relative strength. Azure cloud and Copilot AI products continue to be a positive narrative for the stock. Up 18.2% from your cost base and looking solid.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Hold — GTA 6 fundamentals still strong despite last night's drop
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 3.1% last night but the underlying story is positive — GTA 6 is reportedly tracking near 15 million copies sold and $1.5B in revenue, and Rockstar is already working on a Nintendo Switch 2 version. This looks like market-wide selling, not a company-specific problem. For a long-term holder, this is noise. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Hold — broad tech sell-off, no company-specific bad news
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 2.5% last night as part of a wider NASDAQ decline (down 1.77%). There's no Google-specific news driving this. Down 7.25% from your cost base in total, but the AI and search business remain dominant. No reason to act — long-term case intact.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Hold — AI sector in a rough patch but thesis unchanged
watch_today.detail: GXAI is down 16.6% from your cost base — the toughest performer in your portfolio. Today's 1.8% dip follows last night's NASDAQ weakness. The AI ETF lawsuit (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic face a court bid to freeze advanced AI development) adds short-term noise, but the long-term AI growth story hasn't changed. Painful, but hold.

watch_today.title: Middle East tensions: watch oil & VGE impact this week
watch_today.detail: Iran launched new drone attacks, Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian strikes on US assets, and the USS Roosevelt has arrived in the region. A tanker was also struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz today. Oil fell 2.5% last night but could spike if tensions escalate. This also weighs on emerging markets (your VGE holding) — worth watching through the week.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Hold — small bounce today, but long-term lithium recovery still uncertain
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals popped 1% today but remains down 57% from your cost base. Lithium sector uncertainty continues, with analysts still cautious on the near-term outlook. This is a speculative, long-term bet on the lithium recovery — no reason to panic-sell at these levels, but equally no strong catalyst to add more right now. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA likely done for 2026 — good news for mortgage holders and markets
watch_today.detail: Westpac now says the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) is done raising interest rates for this year. Major banks have already passed on the latest hike. If the RBA pauses, that takes pressure off household budgets and can be a mild positive for the broader ASX. Watch for any official commentary this week.

world.summary: The Middle East is heating up fast — Iran is escalating attacks, a tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, and the USS Roosevelt is now on station. Trump is heading to Asia. Coles confirmed a cyber hack. And Goldman Sachs has laid out its 2027 economic outlook.

stories.title: Iran escalates attacks, Bahrain intercepts strikes, USS Roosevelt arrives in Middle East
stories.why_it_matters: Iran launched new drone attacks over the weekend, with Bahrain claiming it intercepted Iranian strikes targeting US assets in the region. The USS Roosevelt carrier strike group has now arrived in the Middle East, raising fears of a direct US-Iran confrontation. CNN reports Trump is signalling a 'waiting game' rather than immediate retaliation. For everyday Australians, the main risk is oil prices — the Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for about 20% of the world's oil supply, and any blockage there sends petrol prices surging globally.

stories.title: Tanker struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz
stories.why_it_matters: The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) confirmed a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz today — a critical shipping lane connecting the Persian Gulf to the rest of the world. Coming on top of Iranian drone attacks, this is exactly the kind of incident that rattles shipping insurers and oil markets. Crude oil is already down 2.5% from last session but could spike sharply if more vessels are targeted.

stories.title: Trump to embark on Asia trip in final foreign policy push before end of term
stories.why_it_matters: Donald Trump is planning an Asia trip described as a last major foreign policy push before his term ends. The trip is expected to cover relationships with key allies and trading partners in the Indo-Pacific — a region of significant interest to Australia. Any shifts in US posture toward China or other regional powers have direct implications for Australia's trade and security arrangements.

stories.title: Coles confirms it was hacked in a 'cyber security incident'
stories.why_it_matters: Supermarket giant Coles confirmed it has been the victim of a cyber security breach. This is a major headline for Australian consumers — Coles holds personal data on millions of shoppers through its loyalty and payment systems. Details of exactly what data was accessed are still emerging, but it's a reminder to check your Flybuys account and be alert to phishing emails or suspicious activity on linked cards.

stories.title: Goldman Sachs lays out its 2027 economic outlook
stories.why_it_matters: Goldman Sachs has published its economic outlook for 2027, a closely-watched annual forecast from one of the world's biggest investment banks. While the full text isn't available here, these outlooks typically set the tone for how big institutional investors position themselves for the year ahead — covering growth, inflation, interest rates and market returns globally. Worth keeping an eye on for any specific calls on Australia or emerging markets.

markets.summary: A rough night in the US — the NASDAQ dropped 1.77% and the S&P 500 fell 1.29% last night, dragging on ASX futures. The ASX 200 itself closed down 0.41% today. Oil slid 2.46% despite Middle East tensions, and the Aussie dollar weakened against the USD.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Soft session today, down 0.4%. Global uncertainty and last night's US weakness weighed on sentiment.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a broad sell-off — down 1.3%. Risk-off mood dominated.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech bore the brunt last night, with the NASDAQ falling 1.77%. Dragged down AI and growth stocks.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell 2.5% last night despite Middle East tensions — markets may be pricing in a 'waiting game' from Trump. Could swing sharply if the Hormuz situation escalates.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold slipped slightly — a mild surprise given Middle East tensions usually push gold up. Still hovering near record highs above $3,870.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar fell 0.78% — now at 67.5 US cents. A weaker AUD means your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) are worth slightly more in Aussie dollar terms when converted.

politics.summary: Big week in Australian domestic politics — the RBA may be done hiking rates for 2026, Labor faces a Senate battle over its gas bill, CGT reform is gaining traction, and PM Albanese is navigating a tricky meeting with Trump.

stories.title: Westpac says RBA is done hiking rates for 2026
stories.why_it_matters: Westpac economists believe the RBA has finished raising interest rates for this year after the latest hike, which the major banks quickly passed on to mortgage holders. The AFR ran an op-ed arguing rate rises can't fix supply-side shocks like a blocked Strait of Hormuz — adding pressure on the RBA to pause. If Westpac is right, mortgage repayments won't get worse from here this year, which is a relief for millions of Australian households.

stories.title: Greens consider supporting Spender's 40% CGT discount alternative
stories.why_it_matters: Independent MP Zoe Spender has proposed a compromise on Capital Gains Tax (CGT) — reducing the discount investors get on asset sales from 50% to 40% (rather than Labor's proposed 25%). The Greens are now signalling they could support this middle-ground position. CGT reform affects anyone who sells an investment property or shares — a 40% discount would still be more generous than Labor's proposal, but would raise less revenue for the government. This is a live negotiation in Canberra right now.

stories.title: Albanese faces tightrope walk ahead of Trump meeting
stories.why_it_matters: PM Anthony Albanese is preparing to meet Donald Trump and is walking a careful line — he wants the US to stay engaged in the Indo-Pacific for Australia's security, but also wants Trump to push for an end to the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Australia's trade and defence relationships mean Albanese can't afford to alienate Trump, but domestic opinion is very sensitive about being seen to cosying up to him. The meeting will be watched closely for any signals on AUKUS submarines and trade.

stories.title: Labor's gas market bill faces Senate showdown
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's bill to regulate Australia's domestic gas market is heading for a Senate battle, with the Resources Minister expressing frustration at WA's opposition to the scheme. The bill is designed to cap gas prices and ensure domestic supply, but gas producers and some states argue it will discourage investment. This matters for energy bills — if it passes, it could put downward pressure on household and industrial gas prices, but producers say it risks reducing future supply.

stories.title: Renegade Labor MP warns dumping Chalmers would be 'spectacularly stupid self-harm'
stories.why_it_matters: An unnamed Labor backbencher has gone public warning that any push to remove Treasurer Jim Chalmers would be 'spectacularly stupid self-harm' for the government. This signals internal tensions within the Labor Party over economic management, particularly as Australia grapples with stubborn inflation and the RBA's rate hikes. Chalmers is a central figure in the CGT reform debate — his position matters for what ultimately gets legislated.

ai.summary: The biggest AI story today is a new lawsuit seeking to legally freeze advanced AI development by OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and SpaceX. Meanwhile, the EU is renewing its push for global AI rules, and the debate over whether to pursue a binding international treaty or shared voluntary standards is heating up.

stories.title: Lawsuit filed seeking court-ordered freeze on advanced AI development
stories.why_it_matters: A new legal case has been filed against OpenAI, Google (Alphabet), Anthropic and SpaceX, seeking a court order that would freeze the development of advanced AI models. The plaintiffs argue that the pace of AI development poses existential risks and that no democratic process has approved it. This is a landmark legal move — if it gained any traction, it would directly hit your GOOG and GXAI.AX holdings. It's a long shot legally, but it signals a growing organised push to slow AI through the courts rather than just legislation.

stories.title: EU renews push for global AI rules after US midterms weaken Trump
stories.why_it_matters: With Trump's political position weakened by the US midterm elections, the EU is seizing the moment to push harder for binding international AI regulations. Europe has already passed its own AI Act, and Brussels now wants a global framework. If international rules tighten on AI, that could add compliance costs to companies like Google and Microsoft — but it could also create a more stable, trusted environment for AI businesses long-term.

stories.title: Debate: global AI treaty vs shared voluntary standards
stories.why_it_matters: Experts are split on how to govern AI globally. One camp wants a formal UN-style treaty with binding rules — similar to nuclear weapons conventions. The other argues that's too slow and rigid, and that shared voluntary technical standards (like how the internet is governed) would be faster and more practical. The outcome of this debate will shape how much freedom AI companies like Google, Microsoft and OpenAI have to operate over the next decade.

stories.title: UN regulation of AI needs democratic input, advocates say
stories.why_it_matters: Advocacy group Democracy Without Borders is calling for public democratic input into any UN-level AI governance framework, arguing that decisions about AI's limits shouldn't be made by tech companies and governments behind closed doors. The concern is that without public accountability, AI regulation could either be captured by industry (too weak) or by authoritarian governments (too restrictive). This is an emerging civil society push that could shape how global AI rules evolve over the next few years.

sport.summary: The Roosters won the NRL Grand Final in a heart-stopper, 19-18 over the Knights. The 2027 NRL Magic Round draw is confirmed with a blockbuster Broncos v Panthers clash headlining. In AFL, five rule tweaks are confirmed for 2027. And a 14-year-old Gold Coast surfer just made history.

stories.title: Roosters win the 2026 NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters edged out the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a Grand Final classic at Accor Stadium last Sunday. A one-point margin at the final whistle — it doesn't get closer than that. The Roosters claim the premiership in one of the most dramatic Grand Finals in recent memory.

stories.title: 2027 NRL Magic Round draw confirmed — Broncos v Panthers headliner
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL has confirmed the biggest-ever Magic Round schedule for 2027, with Brisbane hosting all 16 clubs across one weekend. The headline game is Brisbane Broncos vs Penrith Panthers — a mouth-watering clash of recent powerhouses. Other confirmed matches include Rabbitohs vs Cowboys (Saturday night), Wests Tigers vs Raiders, and more. If you're on the Gold Coast, it's a road trip worth considering.

stories.title: 14-year-old Gold Coast surfer Leihani Zoric becomes youngest ISA world champion ever
stories.why_it_matters: Gold Coast local Leihani Zoric, just 14 years old, was crowned women's world champion at the ISA World Surfing Games in Peru on Sunday, beating a field of 105 surfers. She is the youngest champion in the event's history. As a Gold Coast resident, this one's right in your backyard — a remarkable achievement from a teenager already at the top of the world.

stories.title: AFL confirms five rule amendments for 2027 season
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL has confirmed five rule changes for the 2027 season, described as minor amendments rather than any major overhaul. The specific changes haven't been detailed in the available text, but the AFL noted no major structural changes are coming — suggesting tweaks to existing rules around scrimmages, interchange or timing rather than wholesale reform. Worth watching the official AFL announcement for the specifics.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner plotting return to tennis in 2027 after 'brilliant' move
stories.why_it_matters: World No.1 Jannik Sinner is being praised for making a 'brilliant' strategic move as he prepares his return to professional tennis in 2027. The article doesn't specify exactly what the move is, but Sinner — who had a disrupted 2026 — is reportedly positioning himself well for a big comeback season. As the dominant force in men's tennis, his return will be a major storyline heading into the Australian Open.
